Low-twist differential-form vanishing on smooth complete intersections via the punctured cone, conormal resolution and Euler contraction; this is a self-contained proof of a known vanishing statement.
Split cubic fourfolds: normal join divisor, reduced Poisson zero scheme, distinct singular scheme, local Pfaffian and modular field, pure ellipticity and generic-rank-four classification.

Smooth positive-dimensional centres: all-order r>=2 lifting at the defining degree d, H^1(I_C^(r-1))=C^{pi_0(C)}/C; the split elliptic double-curve case supplies a nonzero r=3 obstruction, compared specifically with Pym arXiv:1507.05668v1.

Constant-rank divided-commutator kernel, actual-centre distinction under base change, affine Cramer transitions, global even central lift on a coefficient-dependent principal open containing the entire zero section.

Hesse example of different degree-three central ideals under the ambient identity; coordinate covariance, equivariant complement-line selection on the stated opens, and its remaining full-moduli scope.

Affine reductive equivariant lifting: invariant principal neighborhoods of a stable closed subscheme, lifting invariant sections with character twists, and splitting equivariant vector-bundle exact sequences.
All smooth full cubics: a G_0-invariant even good open containing the whole zero section and a G_0-covariant regular central lift whose image generates the central quotient line.
Smooth ternary restriction: a regular equivariant left inverse to directional differentiation, the centring law B_f_prime=(M B_f-C)N^-1, and the full parabolic block-group central lift.
The incompatibility, in general, of fixing pure-central coefficients with all central translations; the Fermat Weyl-symbol obstruction does not assert nonexistence of equivariant lifts.
Fiberwise central regularity, locally split degreewise multiplication, flat central quotient families and AS-Gorenstein invariants; t=eta*h fixes the deformation parameter under group action.

Reduced rank-two Poisson stratum via a nonzero decomposable-trivector incidence and a parabolic associated bundle; the central scalar gerbe and its character splitting when gcd(m,3)=1. For m=2 the base has dimension 17, without a claim about the fixed-nonzero-h image in noncommutative algebra moduli.
Split-fourfold obstruction: 0->I_C^2->I_C^3(3)->i_*J_C^3(3)->0 and the nonzero connecting class delta(g|X) generating H^1(I_C^2)=C.

Research notes: multi-block central-kernel projectivization, regularity using one active filtration and R-freeness, group-equivariant tautological quotients, classical-line dilatation and its restriction to h-regular test bases; the obstruction to a global retraction depending only on a noncone ternary cubic.

Published Bricalli-Favale-Pirola Theorem 3.4 with n=5,k=2: ambient rank<=3 Hessian locus containing a plane is equivalent to a (3,3) splitting, and hence by the manuscript normal form to rank-four Poisson existence.

Explicit smooth cubic F=x0^3+x1^3+sum(z_i^3)-(sum z_i)^3: reducible Hessian determinant; constant symmetrizers diag(a,b,cI4); no rank-three idempotent and therefore no (3,3) splitting after any linear coordinate change.
Effective quotient-group and fppf stabilizer exact sequences; character-twisted degree-one bundle, classical cubic line and relative Proj of the descended commutative limit.

Zero ternary restriction: affine-linear Jacobian bracket over central coefficients, free rank-four Lie algebra with central e0, PBW after e0=1, exact symmetrization/commutator identity, full-t cubic divided kernel O*sym(f) plus pure-central cubics.

General G_0-equivariant choice prescribed on the reduced union (t=0) union (g=0), with Q=1 there and agreement with sym(f); Reynolds lifting and the second invariant shrinking preserve both conditions.

Support-plane-contained rank-two stratum: nonempty exactly for m>=3; smooth irreducible codimension ten in the reduced rank-two stratum; dimension binom(m+5,3)-m^2-3m-18; scalar gerbe and whole-line character descent when gcd(m,3)=1.

Nodal and cuspidal ternary cubics: complete stabilizers, explicit stabilizer-equivariant left inverses, regular descent along the orbit map and extension of the parabolic centering theorem; codimension-two obstruction to a single g-only retraction on the irreducible locus.

Nodal/cuspidal reduced rank-two Poisson strata: smooth nonempty irreducible loci of codimension one/two, dimensions, tautological singular-point line with pullback weight minus one, neutral scalar gerbe, graded multiplicative descent for every m>=2, and the classical relative Proj and Poisson pair.

All rank-two supports: BWB weights (j,j,j,3,0,...,0), all-integer H1 vanishing for Sym3 Q* and O; the affine Gm-torsor and affine smooth-coefficient factor; H1 of O*F plus pure-central cubics and compatible formal lifts.

Stiefel SL3 torsor, codimension N-2 Hartogs extension and Hilbert finite generation; classical constant relation pivots and generic PBW give the invariant degree-three/four Weyl open; exact completion of the finite divided-commutator kernel gives an algebraic lift with the same residue, without assuming kernel local freeness at the cone vertex.

Full H_N=GL_N x Gm covariance via character-twisted Reynolds averaging, opposite-algebra parity, nonvanishing in K/C, and the separate all-degree PBW/domain and degreewise locally split regular central quotient arguments.

Full reduced rank-two Poisson stratum, central scalar gerbe, character theta=(det L)^r lambda^s with Nr-3s=1, and actual graded multiplicative descent. N=5 includes every nonzero Poisson pair on a smooth cubic threefold; base dimension 17.

Full mixed-coefficient and nonzero-Poisson-parameter centering obstruction: a hypothetical covariant complement produces a regular Stiefel left inverse and contradicts Hartogs at the zero matrix; scheme-theoretic freeness of U via absence of linear gradient syzygies, nontrivial torsor and nonaffine quotient.

CMR accepted-version nodal formula, parameter map to symmetric Jacobian relations, polynomial classical normalization, scalar correction for the node swap, and stable alternative retraction. Full all-support and moduli conclusions are not consequences of the finite symbolic check.
material_corrections: The relative forgetful scheme morphism is affine of finite type, not a closed immersion into the base.
Relative rank strata use the simultaneous scalar action (F,P)->(aF,a^-1 P) and reduced structures.
The threefold derived-recovery corollary explicitly assumes left/right noetherian ambient A over C; its central quotient B inherits noetherianity.
Ambient PBW alone does not imply S-freeness of the central quotient; regular highest active symbol is a sufficient condition, and A/(u^3) demonstrates the obstruction.

The semisimple kernel calculation is attributed precisely to Derdzinski--Gal Theorem B; radical elimination from smoothness remains a separate argument. Bondal section 4 supplies the earlier divergence-free homogeneous lift.

Pym arXiv v1 Theorem 1.3 / Proposition 5.7 are contradicted by the proved split cubic fourfold example. The disconnected-centre failure of Lemma 5.5 is exhibited explicitly; no assertion is made about an unverified published or corrected text.
The divided-commutator kernel commutes with arbitrary base change on the constant-rank open, whereas the ordinary centre can enlarge at h-torsion or at h=0.
Two normalized central lifts have transition Omega_j=a_ij Omega_i+c_ij; equality of their classical limits does not force a_ij=1 or equality of their central ideals.
The fixed-coordinate coefficient-family existence theorem does not assert a coefficient-independent parameter open or equivariant descent to the full Poisson moduli stack.

Uncorrected scalar-weight equivariance gives a gerbe family. When gcd(m,3)=1, the character theta=(det N)^r lambda^s with mr-3s=1 removes degree weights, giving actual graded-algebra descent to the stated reduced Poisson stratum open.
The abstract, introduction and ambient-recovery discussion distinguish the 17-dimensional reduced Poisson base from the unproved dimension of the fixed-nonzero-h noncommutative moduli image.

Full-G equivariance generally requires dropping the pure-central-coefficient gauge. The all-support construction now includes reducible, nonreduced and zero restrictions near h=0. Agreement with independently chosen layerwise explicit formulas is not asserted. Multi-block changes remain open. Zero restriction separately has sym(f) for all t.

Pointwise existence of a non-scalar central element is explicitly credited to Etingof--Ginzburg. Mixed quadratic coefficients by themselves are not claimed as new: for invertible Hesse t they can be translated to the existing presentation.

The general lifting obstruction is independent of any literature-error claim and is C^{pi_0(C)}/C; connectedness gives vanishing, while disconnectedness alone does not assert that every section has a nonzero obstruction.
The ambient recovery appendix uses A for the ambient algebra and B for its central quotient, consistently with the quantization part.
The cubic-fourfold Hessian plane lies in ambient P^5, not in X. Hessian reducibility by itself does not imply a rank-four Poisson structure, as shown by the smooth (1,1,4) example.
For every r>=2 the lifting obstruction has the component-constant description only at the defining degree d; for another twist e the relevant group is H^1(I_C^(r-1)(e-d)).
The descended centre is a cubic line subbundle and its homogeneous ideal; a globally chosen generator on the reduced Poisson stack is not asserted.

Tor in the central-linear-extension display uses the right/left module convention. The u variables form a regular sequence in ambient A, not necessarily in its quotient B; on zero restriction Omega mod(u)=0.

The singular-point line uses pullback M^-1, hence scalar weight -1; tensoring degree d with its d-th power removes the algebra weight d. This uses an equivariant line over each stratum, not a character splitting of the constant group. No congruence condition on m is needed on these two strata.

EG Proposition 8.1.1(i), published pp.1407-1408, already supplies a formal centre with prescribed classical residue and does not assume isolated singularities. Its relative and reductive-compatible formal argument is credited; none of those general facts is claimed as new.
Finite completion algebraizes the mod-h residue of a formal kernel element; it does not identify an arbitrarily chosen whole formal series with a rational algebraic expression.
The global centering obstruction permits dependence on every coefficient of the smooth full cubic, nonzero eta and h; it does not contradict the direct full-support central-kernel construction.

The new full-support selection does not assert agreement with earlier stratumwise centres, including sym(F) on zero restriction, nor extension over all h. The descended object is a cubic line and its ideal, not a selected global generator on the stack.

Fermat active cubic with all 25 mixed coefficients independent over QQ; two explicit rational block coordinate changes, of positive and negative active determinant. Checks the left inverse, extraction of B_f_prime=(M B_f-C)N^-1, covariance of the centred cubic, and all three Jacobian brackets with t_prime=lambda*det(M)*t. This is finite in the coordinate changes, not a computational proof of Reynolds existence or full-group equivariance.

Exact identity over the rational function field with independent Hesse and mixed coefficients: the translated cubic including its constant term and all three free-word quadratic relations agree with the stated Etingof--Ginzburg presentation. This does not prove centrality or PBW flatness.

Exact Hessian matrix and determinant identities for one cubic over QQ; 90 equations in 36 constant-matrix variables, rank 33, kernel dimension 3 and span diag(a,b,cI4). The idempotent ranks over C are 0,1,2,4,5,6. Smoothness, the coordinate-invariant projection implication and the Poisson classification are proved in the manuscript, not by this finite computation.

Universal QQ identities with ten independent potential coefficients and t: decreasing monic rules, only critical overlap zyx, all three central commutators, three translated relations and centre translation covariance (already in the free algebra), with three independent shifts. No specialization, parameter inversion or truncation. General linear/scalar covariance, smoothness, AS conditions and stack descent are not computationally checked here.

The tangent conic-line equivariant-left-inverse system has coefficient/augmented ranks 18/19, independently 4/5 after torus restriction. Exact Groebner reductions put a positive power of each variable in both example gradient ideals. Full stabilizer classification, orbit regularity, quantum centrality and moduli descent are mathematical proofs outside this computation.

Exact QQ/Laurent identities for the known general CMR nodal formula: decreasing monic rewrite rules, only critical overlap zyx, all three central commutators, symmetric-Jacobian parameter map, regular polynomial normalization at t=0, prescribed classical residue, scalar/mu3 weights, corrected node-swap covariance and alternative centering. remaining_limits: The Pym comparison is restricted to checked arXiv:1507.05668v1. Published metadata, the accepted-manuscript repository record and ordinary public access routes were checked, but published/accepted full text was not obtained; no claim is made about an unverified correction or its absence.

Brueckmann original proofs (1976 Satz 3 / 1977 Satz 6) were not obtained; Fu--Hwang Lemma 4.1 and its attribution were verified. The needed low-twist vanishing is proved self-containedly in the manuscript, so these unavailable proofs are no longer a mathematical dependency of that criterion.

Comprehensive novelty of the all-dimensional normal form, component theorem, full quantization combination and all-support algebraic selection is not established. Known formal centres, explicit nodal formulas, BWB, invariant theory, completion and descent are distinguished from their current applications.

The all-support central lift includes all ternary restriction types near the full h=0 section, but no agreement with previously chosen stratumwise formulas or extension over the whole h line is asserted. A regular all-coefficient equivariant centering is impossible; the direct central-kernel construction avoids it.

Actual full reduced rank-two graded descent is proved when gcd(N,3)=1. For 3 dividing N the stated character method fails, without proving nonneutrality or impossibility of other descent methods. Node/cusp strata still have their separate singular-point-line descent in all stated dimensions.

The final full-support theorem excludes zero Poisson structure P=0; this is distinct from its inclusion of the deformation zero section h=0. Multiple-block decomposition and pure-central allocation changes remain outside the global rank-two construction.

For cubic threefolds, 17 is the dimension of the entire reduced nonzero Poisson-pair base. Generic finiteness or a 17-dimensional image for abstract noncommutative algebras at a fixed nonzero h is not proved.

Quantization over the full Poisson moduli stack including multiple blocks, qgr smoothness for all closed parameters and relative residual equivalence through the commutative special point are not claimed.

Only the new CMR nodal verifier was executed for A-v59. Thirteen earlier computations are retained without rerun with current script and certificate hashes checked; proof reading and finite exact checks are not formal verification.
